title: JavaScript gets language semantics, not network authority
summary: The ECMAScript engine is a pluggable execution provider beneath Virtual Browser. Browser host objects remain controlled by Virtual Browser and all network activity is mediated by API Client.
invariants: The ECMAScript engine must not receive independent socket authority.
fetch, XMLHttpRequest, navigation, form submission and script loading pass through Virtual Browser host objects and API Client.
document, window, cookies, storage, timers and events are Virtual Browser-owned host semantics.
Foreign Runtime supplies the native runtime-binding substrate; it does not grant web-origin authority.
Engine replacement must not change placement, egress, WLU, rate or observation authority boundaries.

provenance.claim: API Client provides the outbound request/session/transport seam used by higher-level adapters.
Foreign Runtime v0.22.6 provides ABI-native C scalar aliases for portable native bindings.
